---
title: "Companion curriculum"
subtitle: "The teaching modules of the EU-frames case"
---

The course is built around one exercise: you reproduce a recorded result, vary the analysis behind it, declare one analysis before you run it, and read your result against those of the class. On this site the exercise is taught on the EU-frames case, a panel of 270 country-years built from sixteen Eurobarometer waves, on which a published claim links the economic performance of a country to the terms in which its citizens frame the European Union, and the [case study](../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd) tells it in full. A single day has room for that exercise and little else, so the skills around it are taught in these fourteen modules, which run from R and the IDE to a reanalysis that you can deposit and register. Each module stands on its own, so you can take the one you need and leave the rest.

Every module is written for this case. The modules that run code compute their numbers from the files of the case in `cases/eu-frames/data/` when the page is built, so that a module can be read as a worked analysis as well as an explanation, and you can check each number against your own output. The models that need the respondents themselves, whose Eurobarometer files may not be passed on, were fitted once on the licensed files, and the modules display the saved output of those models beside the code that produced it, while the modules on multilevel models and on simulation work on a simulated twin of the respondents that the course ships.

Nothing here is required for the one-day workshop, which runs in full without any module and with no account to create. Its pages point at some modules as preparation, at others as the slower companion of a part of the day, and at the rest as reading for afterwards. The [Extended course](../tracks/eu-frames-extended/index.qmd) teaches some of them as the sessions of its first and third days, and the [self-study track](../tracks/self-study/index.qmd) reads the modules in its stages, between the tasks of the case.

The modules fall into the three groups of the Companion menu. The first holds the computational tools with which an analysis is written, the second the data and the public records that let others find an analysis and run it again, and the third the statistical methods with which the case is analysed. Within each group the order is roughly the order of what each module assumes.

## Tools {#sec-tools}

The modules on the tools are on the umbrella site of the course, written once for the four cases on the data of the housing-audit case: [Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html) with its [second part](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r-further.html), [Positron and other IDEs](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html). Two modules of this site take the same tools to the panel and the workspace of the EU-frames case:

- [R on the country-year panel](intro-r.qmd) – the files of the case and the routes by which they arrive, the grammar of graphics on the panel of the case, and reading its specification curve.
- [The workspace in the IDE](ide.qmd) – six steps through the workspace of the case, in whichever IDE you chose.

## Data and sharing {#sec-sharing}

- [Social science data sources](data-sources.qmd) – the three routes by which data reach a researcher, a map of the archives, surveys, panels and statistics with the access rule for each, the routes of the case from the GESIS archive, the World Bank, Eurostat and the OSF, and citing data.
- [Building the analysis file](data-management.qmd) – the steps that every build shares, and the country-year panel of the case built from sixteen Eurobarometer waves: the respondent file, the scales and the three scoring rules, the respondent who named nothing, the averaging into country-years and the macro series, each checked against the files that the course committed.
- [Reproducibility repositories](repositories.qmd) – what a repository has to do, the repositories that researchers use, the versions of a record, the SCORE dossier and the Multi100 records of the paper, the OSF after 2026, registrations and preregistration templates, and depositing a reanalysis of your own.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

- [Panel data](panel-data.qmd) – the estimators of the country-year panel: the country-year level, the linear model, clustered standard errors, fixed effects in their two designs and what each absorbs, standard errors with few clusters, random effects, and the within–between model, which separates the change within a country from the differences between countries.
- [Multilevel models](multilevel.qmd) – respondents in country-years in countries, with the models named side by side in the vocabularies of four disciplines: the level of analysis, the simulated twin of the respondents and its limits, random intercepts and random slopes, variance components, the within–between model as group-mean centring, the published model, individual effects against aggregate associations, two designs, survey weights, bounded outcomes, and the second claim of the paper, on the education gap.
- [Binary outcomes](binary-outcomes.qmd) – one survey item as a yes-or-no outcome among respondents grouped in country-years: logit and probit side by side, errors clustered by country-year, average marginal effects, the national unemployment rate between and within countries, an interaction, and a random intercept.
- [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](dags.qmd) – what a causal graph commits you to, confounders, mediators and colliders, the graph of the case and its adjustment set, what fixed effects cannot absorb, the bailout on the graph, what no statistic computed from the data can settle, and a graph of your own.
- [The items behind the scales](measurement.qmd) – the instrument behind every outcome of the menu: the thirteen items and the theory behind their grouping, how the items hang together, exploratory and confirmatory factor structures, reliability, and what all of this means for the menu and for the outcome on the curve.
- [Weights](weighting.qmd) – survey weights inside a country-year cell, the effective sample size, precision weights across cells and population weights across countries, why only the population weight changes the estimand, the reproduced specification under each weight, and weights in estimation.
- [Missing answers](missingness.qmd) – what a respondent who mentions no frame at all does to a share built from mentions, the three mechanisms of missingness, the rules that the menu offers and what each assumes, multiple imputation, "don't know" as an answer, and the sensitivity of the result to the assumption.
- [Bayesian estimation](bayesian.qmd) – the model of the claim stated as a posterior distribution: prior, likelihood and posterior, priors for the two-way design and what they imply, the posterior of the slope, errors that persist within a country from year to year, partial pooling of the country slopes, sensitivity to the priors, and the slope across the models.
- [Meta-analysis](meta-analysis.qmd) – what a meta-analysis combines, the common scale on which Multi100 put the results of its analysts, the five analysts of the case on that scale and their five analyses of one dataset combined, the two-way slope as a weighted average of the 27 country slopes, and other studies of many analysts.
- [Simulation as a method](simulation.qmd) – the simulated twin of the respondents, its recipe and its validation, composition against context, and a world in which the true effect is zero.
- [The multiverse and its critics](multiverse.qmd) – where multiverse analysis came from, the purposes that a multiverse can serve, the debate of 2025–26, frequency against probability, robustness against replicability, and the curve of the case with its pruned menu, its fork chart and the displays of heterogeneity and influence.

The reading on [the specification curve](../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) of the case, on what a test of the curve as a whole can and cannot establish, belongs with these modules without being one of them.

## Pages on the AR4DS site {#sec-umbrella}

The material that does not change with the case lives on the [AR4DS site](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/), the umbrella site of the course, and the modules link to it where it is needed. The [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) installs R, Quarto, an IDE and the workspace, with the [setup help](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) beside it. The modules on the tools listed [above](#sec-tools) teach R, the IDE and Quarto, the format in which the report of the exercise is written, and [Git and GitHub for reproducible research](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html) puts a reanalysis of your own under version control and shares it on GitHub.
